newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina says to take over Caltex field.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina says to take over Caltex field.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina said on Monday it would take over the Coastal Plain Pakanbaru (CPP) block operated by PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia in 2001.
"We have sent a letter to Caltex that we are going to take over the CPP block after the contract expires in 2001," Pertamina president director Faisal Abda'oe told a parliamentary commission.
"Pertamina has the capability to operate the block, including technology and funding," Abda'oe said.
The CPP block, located in the central part of Sumatra Island, was under a 30 year-contract with Caltex from 1971.
Abda'oe said Pertamina has made preparations to further develop the field.
"Currently the field produces around 77,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude oil. We will further develop the field with and possibly enhance oil recovery," Abda'oe said.
He said Caltex had sent a letter to Pertamina asking for the extension of the contract.
"Pertamina has rejected Caltex's demand for extension," he said.
Caltex, joinly owned by Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, currently operates across some 31,000 sq km in central Sumatra.
Caltex production across Indonesia is about 770,100 bpd of crude, about half of the country's total output.
